title: Common doctrine: God's eternal will is the cause of all things, and human acts too fall under his immutable decrees
source_text: THESIS I. COmmunis & recepta Theologorum doctrina est, eaque ex Scripturae manifestis documentis hausta, aeternam Dei voluntatem esse rerum omnium causam; ac immutabilibus providentiae Divinae Decretis omnia subjacere, etiam actus humanos; neque quicquam, non tantum a causis brutis sive inanimis, sed etiam ab hominibus & Angelis fieri, nisi secundum aeternam Dei praeordinationem & determinationem.
pass_a_gloss: THESIS I. The common and received doctrine of Theologians is, and that drawn from manifest documents of Scripture, that the eternal will of God is the cause of all things; and that all things are subject to the immutable Decrees of divine providence, even human acts; and that nothing is done, not only by brute or inanimate causes, but also by men and Angels, except according to the eternal preordination and determination of God.
pass_b_english: It is the common, accepted teaching of theologians, drawn from the plain witness of Scripture, that God's eternal will is the cause of all things. Everything, human acts included, is subject to the unchangeable decrees of God's providence.
Nothing happens, whether by brute and lifeless causes or by men and angels, except in accordance with God's eternal preordination and determination.
